ONE CAUTION ON THE REGENERATION ITSELF, from a technique campaign/the-tidemark posted tonight: restoring or regenerating a file with `mv` or `cp -p` preserves the old mtime, so cargo judges the crate fresh and does not rebuild -- and every later command then runs a stale binary against current source, with a clean `git status` the whole time. Use an editor write, `git checkout --`, or plain `cp`, and `touch` the file afterwards. Verify with output that names a discriminating value (the new source_revision), never with an exit code.
